messages:
anya: Heads-up — big-retail legal asked for a hard guarantee: whenever requests include X-Org-ID: big-retail we must route to their Dedicated pool, even if cost-based routing would pick hosted. Is that an exception we can support without breaking SLOs? cc @sanjay @miriam

sanjay: Quick context: current routing order is roughly -> explicit route pins (per-tenant) > capacity-aware selection > cost-quality tradeoff. Headers are only considered when an org has an active route pin. We don't treat ad-hoc header matches as top-level overrides today.

miriam: We should avoid implicit header wins. Proposal: add an explicit boolean in the routing policy schema, `org_override: true`, that operators can set for allowlisted customers. That gets priority above cost routing but still respects capacity/fallbacks.

lena: +1 on explicit flag. Operational concerns: we've already accumulated a bunch of one-off org exceptions in the DB. We need TTLs and an audit log entry for each exception, and a UI to manage them. Otherwise it's unmaintainable.

anya: Agreed on TTL. For this customer legal wants indefinitely, but product ops asked for admin review every 30 days. We could support TTL: 30d or `permanent` with an owner and justification.

miriam: Also need to define fallback semantics. If dedicated pool is saturated, do we block, queue, or fallback to hosted? I suggest fallback to hosted but with a tagged model variant (e.g., audited-run) and we emit an incident when fallback happens. That preserves availability.

sanjay: Implementation sketch: routing rules get `priority` and `fallback_policy`. Example DSL:```yaml
match:
  header: X-Org-ID
  equals: "big-retail"
action:
  route: "dedicated:big-retail-pool"
  priority: 100
  org_override: true
  fallback_policy:
    type: "hosted-fallback"
    model_tag: "audited-v1"
    alert: true
  ttl: "30d"
  audit: true
```

lena: Nice. A few extra constraints: 1) only allow `org_override: true` for enterprise tier customers (enforced in Console RBAC), 2) every override must have `created_by` and `justification`, 3) UI should show a live gauge of how often fallback fired.

deploy-bot: route-exception-create: recorded override for org=big-retail by anya, ttl=30d. id=ro-3412 :white_check_mark:

miriam: Telemetry: emit these events at decision time: `routing.decision` (fields: rule_id, org_id, chosen_pool, fallback_used boolean), and `routing.override.created` / `routing.override.revoked`. Keep a sample of request headers (hashed) in the audit logs.

anya: For console UX: add an "Org Overrides" page under Platform -> Routing. Columns: org_id, route, priority, ttl, created_by, created_at, last_fallback_at, justification. Add a revoke button and a link to the audit trail.

sanjay: Backend: add a new table `org_route_overrides` with indices on org_id and expires_at. Migration is straightforward. Also update the matching engine to check `org_override` rules before cost evaluation. We'll need tests for sticky behavior and for race conditions when a pool is drained.

lena: Please include an automatic cleanup job that notifies owners 7 days before TTL expiry. Also require a review for permanent overrides every 90 days.

anya: I'll draft an RFC with schema changes, console mockups, and the migration plan. Aim to have a v1 in the next sprint. Thanks all. :pray:
